lesson_title: DD-only overlay without VT is strictly inferior for weak-alpha strategies
lesson: Removing VT and using only DD brake (10/25) on a weak base signal (SR 0.633) produces the worst outcome in the STR_1422 mutation family: SR 0.566, OOS retention 15.8%, alpha trend ratio 0.21 (near-zero recent alpha). Without VT's vol compression, the DD brake must activate more frequently against raw volatility, creating a worse timing signal. The DD-only hypothesis -- that simpler overlays are more robust -- is disproven for this factor pair. DD-only works better when the base signal has strong alpha (SR > 1.0) where vol compression would waste good returns. For weak signals (SR < 0.8), VT's vol compression at least maintains a marginally positive SR by reducing the denominator.
actionable_rule: DD-only overlays should be reserved for base signals with SR > 1.0. For SR < 0.8, always combine DD with VT to at least maintain the SR through vol compression.
